skills.title: My Roles and Responsibilities
skills.description: You can be a student, a friend, a family member, and a pet owner. Pick the jobs and responsibilities that go with each of your roles.

skills.title: How Roles Change
skills.description: Your roles can change in different places and as you get older. Match what people do at home, at school, and at work.

skills.title: Big Events Change Roles
skills.description: Starting school, a new baby, or a family tradition can change what you do. Match each event to how a role or responsibility changes.

skills.title: Comparing Life Events
skills.description: Kids and families have some of the same events and some different ones. Sort events into ones that are alike and ones that are different.

skills.title: Putting My Life in Order
skills.description: Things happen to you one after another, like crawling, walking, then riding a bike. Put events from your life in the right order.

skills.title: How We Affect Each Other
skills.description: What we do can make others feel happy, sad, proud, or safe. Pick how an action changes the way someone feels about themselves.

skills.title: Reviving Indigenous Identity
skills.description: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit people are bringing back languages, ceremonies, and family ties. Pick the ways they do this and why it makes them proud.

skills.title: Important People, Places, Things
skills.description: Some people, places, and things matter a lot in your life. Match each one to its job or purpose.

skills.title: Kind and Inclusive Actions
skills.description: Sharing, cooperating, being polite, and caring for Elders and nature are good actions. Sort the actions that are kind and welcoming.

skills.title: Respecting People and Earth
skills.description: We should treat people and the environment with respect. Pick the ways to show respect, like taking turns or saving water.

skills.title: Natural and Built Features
skills.description: Communities have natural things like rivers and forests, and built things like roads and libraries. Sort them into natural or built.

skills.title: Areas in My Community
skills.description: Communities have homes areas, shopping areas, busy roads, and natural areas. Match each area to what it looks like.

skills.title: Land My School Is On
skills.description: Every school sits on traditional Indigenous land and treaty territory. Pick the territory your school is on.

skills.title: Community Services and Workers
skills.description: Post offices, clinics, and stores have workers who help people. Match each service or job to the need it meets.

skills.title: How Places Meet Our Needs
skills.description: People use nature, buildings, and services to get what they need. Pick what could happen if one of them was missing.

skills.title: Who Runs Community Services
skills.description: The government or community runs services like fire, police, and garbage pickup. Match each service to what people must do to help.

skills.title: Caring for My Community
skills.description: We can put garbage in the right bins, plant gardens, and join clean-ups. Pick the actions that help the local environment and how they help.

skills.title: Near, Far, Left, Right
skills.description: We describe where places are with words like near, far, left, right, in front, and behind. Pick the words that tell where a place is.

skills.title: Parts of a Map
skills.description: Maps have a title, symbols, a legend, directions, and colours. Label the parts of a simple map and tell what they show.

skills.title: Measuring with Footsteps and Tiles
skills.description: We can measure distance with footsteps, tiles, or blocks. Pick which unit fits and which measure is longer.

skills.title: Making a Simple Map
skills.description: A map uses symbols and units like blocks to show places and distances. Choose the right symbols and put places in the right spots on a map.
